correctness.rationale: For n=p², gcd(p²+p+1,p)=1 would force p²+p+1|p−1, impossible. For n=2q distinct primes, (q+1)|2q(q−1) gives q+1|4, hence q=3, and n=6 works. For odd p<q write A=(p+1)/2, B=(q+1)/2. Exact divisibility is AB|pq(A−1)(B−1). Since gcd(B,q(B−1))=1, B|p(A−1); and gcd(A,p(A−1))=1, A|q(B−1). Since q>A prime, A|B−1. With B>A>A−1 and gcd(p,A−1)=1, B=pd for d|A−1. Because p≡−1 mod A, A|d+1 forces d=A−1. Thus q=p(p−1)−1. Conversely B=p(A−1), gcd(A,B)=1, B|p(A−1), A|B−1, and exact original condition follows. This covers all n with Ω(n)=2 and makes no claim about infinitely many such prime pairs.
